page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the t2d server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor using the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-4 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring in the top 25% on stress-ng single-core tests. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth align with average mid-tier expectations, with uncached read and write bandwidths measuring 48.77 GB/sec and 34.91 GB/sec respectively. Software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing benchmarks also fall within the average range. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput, both scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio offer reliable, non-burstable compute resources for general-purpose workloads. It is well-suited for applications requiring consistent single-core execution, such as lightweight database operations, software compilation, and moderate text or image processing tasks. The lack of local storage and GPU acceleration makes it less suitable for high-throughput storage-heavy databases or intensive deep learning workloads.
